Paper: [Girshick (2015), Fast R-CNN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.08083).

## Problem

[R-CNN](r-cnn.qmd) runs a CNN separately on many overlapping image crops and trains its classifier and box regressors in separate stages.
Fast R-CNN shares the convolutional computation across regions and trains the classification and localization heads together.

## Previous Attempts

R-CNN establishes the value of pretrained CNN features for region-based detection.
Spatial pyramid pooling methods show how regions can share a whole-image feature map.
Fast R-CNN combines region pooling with a differentiable multi-task detection network. [Sections 1–2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1504.08083#page=2).

## Proposed Solution

The backbone processes the whole image once to produce a convolutional feature map.
An external proposal method supplies regions of interest, or RoIs.
For each RoI, **RoI pooling** divides its projected feature-map region into a fixed grid and max-pools each bin independently for every channel.
The resulting fixed-size features pass through fully connected layers and branch into a class softmax and class-specific box offsets. [Section 2.1 and Figure 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1504.08083#page=2).

Pooling acts on shared features, not on a separately resized raw-image crop.
Its quantized regions and bins are also distinct from the later RoIAlign operation.
Image features are shared across proposals, while each region still receives its own pooled representation and predictions.

## Joint Classification and Localization

Let $u$ be a region's class label, with $u=0$ denoting background.
Let $p$ be the predicted class distribution, $t^u$ the predicted box offsets for class $u$, and $v$ the target offsets.
The region loss is

$$
    \begin{aligned}
        L&=L_{\mathrm{cls}}+\lambda\mathbf1[u\ge1]L_{\mathrm{loc}},\\
        L_{\mathrm{cls}}&=-\log p_u,\\
        L_{\mathrm{loc}}&=\sum_k\rho(t_k^u-v_k).
    \end{aligned}
$$

Background regions contribute classification loss but no foreground box-regression loss.
The offsets follow the center-and-log-size parameterization described in [R-CNN](r-cnn.qmd#box-regression).
The robust penalty is Smooth L1:

$$
    \rho(r)=
    \begin{cases}
        \tfrac12r^2,& |r|<1,\\
        |r|-\tfrac12,& |r|\ge1.
    \end{cases}
$$

It is quadratic near zero and linear for larger residuals, avoiding the unbounded residual-proportional slope of squared loss. [Section 2.3, Equations 1–3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1504.08083#page=3).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false" title="Training details: region sampling and feature sharing"}
The paper samples a small number of images, then multiple RoIs from each image, so those regions share the expensive backbone computation.
Its standard recipe samples 25% foreground RoIs with IoU at least 0.5 and selects background RoIs from the interval $[0.1,0.5)$.
These are minibatch construction choices, not the definition of Smooth L1 or universal thresholds for every detector. [Section 2.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1504.08083#page=3).
:::

## Evidence and Limitations

The paper evaluates detection accuracy, training time, and inference time against earlier region-based systems. [Section 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1504.08083#page=4).
The shared feature map removes repeated CNN processing of image crops, but the detector still depends on external proposals.
Its inference-time SVD option approximates a large fully connected matrix by two lower-rank linear maps without inserting a new nonlinearity between them. [Section 2.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1504.08083#page=4).
This compression is an optional speed optimization, separate from RoI pooling and the multi-task loss.

## Connections

[Faster R-CNN](faster-r-cnn.qmd) replaces the external proposal generator with a learned region proposal network.
The [loss note](../../study-notes/machine-learning/loss.qmd#huber) explains the quadratic-to-linear robust penalty, and [cross-entropy](../../study-notes/mathematics/entropy.qmd#cross-entropy) explains the class term.
